mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns higher over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4%, it signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops below 4% but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 20-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with increasing payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong economy, boosting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both INDPRO and PAYEMS grow but SPX returns are negative in over 40% of the 20-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when FEDFUNDS exceed 4.5%, higher interest rates negatively impact equity valuations, leading to lower S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are above 4.5% but SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of the next 5-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts (HOUST) reflect strong consumer demand, which positively influences corporate revenues and S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of the 60-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth exceeds 5% but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of the 20-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI (CPIAUCSL) is high and FEDFUNDS increase, inflation combined with higher rates may slow economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If CPI is high and FEDFUNDS rise but SPX returns are positive in over 40% of the 5-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime with low unemployment (UNRATE < 4%) and rising payroll employment (PAYEMS), the strong labor market boosts economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 4% and PAYEMS grows but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of the 20-day periods, the hypothesis fails.
